    The banquet ended and the room was quickly cleared to make room for the staging of an old-time "levee" designed to give pleasure to the young people who attended the banquet as well as to provide the ex-students extra time for long-wished-for-visits among the participants. The levee, carried on under the direction of Robert and Harry Naylor of Sherman in the absence of the Naylor boys of Collinsville, afforded an excellent means of adding to the socialization of the ex-students, who were the "onlookers only" as no one was permitted to be on the floor but those who wore the official ex-student registration badge. The dignity and solemnity with which Robert Naylor directed the old Scotch Reel, lent all the more jollity to the affair. With the approach of midnight it was "goodnight, ladies" and the crowd left the Halsell Memorial Gymnasium not to return until two o'clock dedication ceremonies the next day.

THE DEDICATION OF THE HALSELL MEMORIAL GYMNASIUM—Sunday morning, August 7, 1938, services at all the churches in Savoy were attended by many ex-students, and the Reverend May, pastor of the Sherman Avenue Church, preached at the Baptist Church. In addition to attending these services, many of the visitors took advantage of opportunity to visit in the town of Savoy in search of familiar landmarks of the past. Many of the participants in the reunion marked their first return to these scenes in forty or fifty years.

    At two o'clock, in the gymnasium, the formal dedication program began. Dr. William Deatherage of Dallas, delivered the invocation. He is the only son of Dr. J. R., living, being then an octogenarian.

    Honorable J. B. May, Mayor of Savoy, made the address of welcome and Honorable Mark McMahon, of Fort Worth, responded.
